reason: 'bracts ... many-veined': veins (vascular bundle PO_0005020, synonym 'vein') are present in large numbers on the bract (container PO_0009055). This matches the flora.
'Herbs annual or biennial': the whole plant has an annual or a biennial life span, given as alternatives.

target: female (PATO:0000383) as a context quality of the inflorescence
fix: A sex word before the part ('Female inflorescences', '♂ flowers') sets a sex context that should go into the bearer context. The male and female inflorescences are described separately here.
reason: The flora says only the female inflorescences are few-flowered. Read without the sex, the annotation also covers the male inflorescences, which are described separately with their own stamens.

target: involucral bract (PO_0009045) would be more exact
fix: 'phyllary' is a synonym of involucral bract (PO_0009045). Grounding it to that class would be more exact than plain bract.
reason: The phyllaries are imbricate, and a phyllary is a bract, so the annotation is true. The more specific class is available.
Corolla 3.2–5 mm long.

fix: In mosses, 'teeth' after 'exostome', 'endostome' or 'peristome' are peristome teeth (PO_0030043) themselves, not leaf or phyllome lamina teeth inside them.
reason: Exostome teeth are the outer peristome teeth of the moss capsule. The count of 16 is of the peristome teeth. Phyllome lamina tooth (a leaf-margin tooth) is the wrong part.
The spikelet clusters (the inflorescence units) are sometimes more or less confluent, that is, run together or fused. 'Connate' with the frequency word 'sometimes' is a fair reading.
'branches alternate, numerous': there are many branches.
Stamens 20.
'bracteoles ... 1–2 mm long'.
The two basal bracteoles are ovate. The basal context (FLOPO_0991002) is kept, which matters because the apical ones are lanceolate.
'bracts ... acutish': acutish means subacute.
The panicle branches are higher-order inflorescence axes, and they are erect or obliquely ascending.
In 'Plants 0.5-3(-3.5) × 0.5-3(-5) dm' the first dimension is the height: 5–30 cm, up to 35 cm. The unit conversion is correct.

target: leaf lamina base (PO_0008019); quality obtuse/roundish (PATO_0001935) or truncated (PATO_0000936)
fix: In 'round/rounded ... at base' the shape belongs to the base of the lamina (PO_0008019), not the whole lamina. Here 'round' means a rounded base (obtuse/roundish), not an orbicular blade.
reason: The flora says the base is rounded or truncate. The annotation says the whole blade is orbicular or truncated, which is false (the blade is ovate to lanceolate). Both the part and the reading of 'round' are wrong.

target: a place slot 'on the veins' (leaflet abaxial veins)
fix: In 'pubescent on the veins ... below' the place word 'on the veins' limits the hairs to the veins of the lower surface. The place slot should hold it, or the bearer should be the vein.
reason: The hairs on the lower side of the leaflet are only on the veins. Dropping that makes the whole lower surface pubescent, which the flora does not say.

fix: When 'above'/'below' follows a lamina quality, the quality belongs to that surface. Here 'above' means the upper (adaxial) surface.
reason: Only the upper surface is lustrous or dull; the lower surface is dull and brownish. Annotating the whole leaf merges the two different surfaces.
Leaf blade 0.5-1.8 × 0.5-1.8 cm: the first number is the length.
The cymes (inflorescences) are usually shorter than the petioles.

target: position: outer (of the cypselae in the head)
fix: In 'Cypselae: outer ..., ± erect; inner ...' the qualities after 'outer' hold only for the outer members of the series. The position slot must carry 'outer'.
reason: Only the outer cypselae are said to be nearly straight and ± erect. The inner ones are described separately (papillate).
The stamens are as long as the perianth (ratio 1).
Petals 3.5-4.5 by 1-2.5 cm: the length is 3.5–4.5 cm.
The secondary stems are not tomentose. Leaving out 'secondary' does not make this false, since the primary stems are not called tomentose either.

fix: '36 mm' between '8-15 mm long' and 'acute' is a range whose dash was lost in the source, so reading it as 3–6 mm is right.
reason: A bract 8–15 mm long cannot be 36 mm wide. The source clearly lost the dash, and 3–6 mm is the intended width.
The blade ranges from triangular (PATO_0001875) to hastate (PATO_0104352).
The monochasium (inflorescence) has 2–5 flowers.

fix: In 'X covered with fibrous Y remains' the quality belongs to Y (here the scale leaves of the rhizome), not to X.
reason: The fibrous things are the grey-brown remains of scale leaves that cover the rhizome. The rhizome itself is not called fibrous.
The lateral leaflets are 1–3.8 cm long. The lateral context (FLOPO_0991380) is kept; 'when present' is only a condition.

target: oblong-elliptic (oblong PATO_0000946 combined with elliptic PATO_0000947) as the start of the range
fix: A hyphenated shape compound ('oblong-elliptic') must not be cut down to its first word. It is an intermediate shape (oblong and elliptic) and should be kept whole as the end of a range.
reason: The range starts at oblong-elliptic, but the start value is plain oblong, which loses 'elliptic'. The end, oblanceolate, is correct.

fix: 'Fleurs: ♂ en panicules' gives a sex context (♂ = male). It must go into the bearer context, the same way as 'female'/'♀'.
reason: Only the male flowers are in panicles. Without the sex, the annotation says the plant bears panicles in general, which may not hold for the female flowers.
